claims.text: The artifacts that carry the distance question all describe one and the same trip: trip_id TRP-02817 appears on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown alike; the trace's first fix (2026-08-10T07:28:09+08:00) is the recorded trip_started timestamp, and the fare was charged at 07:47:14, after the recorded trip end at 07:46:49. The rider's identification limb under POL-RD-08 is satisfied on the platform's own telemetry.

The rider pleaded the governing field, and the governing field confirms the detour: POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the measure, the trace runs 14.39 km against the 12.0 km optimal stored on the trip record, and the excess is 2.39 km. The trip record's 14.4 km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and under POL-RD-01 may not be cited for the threshold test; the rider has not cited it.

The establishment test is not met on the field as published, and the rider does not pretend otherwise: the trace excess of 2.39 km clears the absolute limb (well above 0.8 km) but is 19.92% of the 12.0 km optimal, some 10 metres short of the 20% limb, so POL-RD-01's percentage test fails and no deviation is established. The rider does not ask the tribunal to read 19.92% as 'greater than 20%', and does not press a distance refund as of right.

The driver's only explanation — "Minor detour because of a road works sign" — cannot be weighed, and I disclose the impairment on its face: no traffic advisory covers this trip, EV-ADVIS-02817-01 being MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT. POL-RD-03 therefore cannot be run, no closure-adjusted optimal can be produced, and under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08 an uncited traffic assertion neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended route; the driver names no artifact and no clause at all.

Nothing on this record excludes any part of the measured excess. The chat log holds 0 messages, so there is no rider instruction capable of engaging POL-RD-04; neither pickup_amended_at nor dropoff_amended_at is set and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 does not re-apply the threshold against amended endpoints; and vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply and 12.0 km remains the only optimal on the record.

If the tribunal finds the establishment test satisfied, the refund is arithmetic and is 2.56 before rounding: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 12.0 + 0.28 x 16.0) x 1.0 — the surge multiplier read from the fare breakdown, which is where POL-RD-02 says it must be read — plus 0.80 platform fee, nil ERP, nil fixed surcharge, nil waiting fee, less nil promo, giving 18.08; refund = 20.64 - 18.08 = 2.56, payable rounded up to SGD 2.60.

That refund is neither de minimis nor full: 2.56 is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so this is not a NO_ACTION case on quantum, and it is 12.4% of the 20.64 charged, below the 90% share that would make it a FULL_REFUND; it is also far below the SGD 150 figure that forces escalation under POL-RD-10. On that arithmetic the rider's ask is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 2.60 out of the SGD 3.00 contested.

The deviation gate has two limbs and the percentage limb fails. The rider's own headline figures prove the shortfall rather than the deviation. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure of 14.39 km govern over the trip record's 14.4 km, which is a rounded convenience copy that may not be cited for the threshold test; and even on that rounded copy the excess is exactly 2.40 km, precisely 20.0% of 12.0 km, which is still not 'greater than 20%'. On either figure the percentage limb fails.

I concede the absolute limb: 2.39 km does exceed the 0.8 km floor in POL-RD-01. But POL-RD-01 requires BOTH tests to pass, and only one does. A single satisfied limb cannot carry the rider's case, and the missing limb, the percentage limb, cannot be supplied from anything on this record.

The trace is clean and unimpaired for policy purposes, so this case can be ruled on it without any of the gap-handling consequences. It carries 113 fixes over roughly 18 minutes 40 seconds at a 10-second sample interval, with 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. None of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is met, no independent corroboration is required, and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The initial burden is the rider's and it is not discharged. POL-RD-08 requires the rider to show, citing evidence, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold. The only artifacts that measure this trip, the trace and the booking optimal, put the excess at 2.39 km and 19.92%, below the threshold, so the burden never shifts to the driver and the driver need not reach any exculpatory clause at all.

The only route to money that survives a failed establishment test is a pass-through or billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09, and there is nothing to correct. The fare ledger shows no ERP gantry lines, no tolls and no airport surcharge, and no charge line lacking a counterpart in the trip record: it is meter arithmetic on 14.4 km at $0.75 per km plus 18.7 minutes at $0.28 per minute plus the $0.80 platform fee. POL-RD-09(4) affords the rider nothing on these facts.

NO_ACTION is both the correct outcome and, in this dispute, the outcome favourable to the driver. The dispute is rider-filed, and the fare breakdown records payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00. POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative and leaves that state exactly as it is: the charge stands and no money moves to the rider.

The driver's counterparty note that there was a minor detour because of a road works sign is not offered as an exoneration and does not alter the arithmetic: a minor detour is exactly what a 2.39 km, 19.92% excess looks like. A narrative sentence in a party statement is not a measurement and cannot substitute for the POL-RD-01 test or establish a deviation the trace does not show.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the disputed charge is SGD 20.64 and the amount contested is SGD 3.00. This is a rider-filed ROUTE_DEVIATION dispute and the outcome is NO_ACTION — the charge stands and no money moves to either side.

The gate. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess over the optimal route is BOTH greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km. The governing measurement is the GPS trace: gps_trace.trace_distance_km 14.39 km against the booked optimal of 12.0 km (trip record) is an excess of 2.39 km, or 19.92% of optimal. The trip record's 14.4 km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for the threshold test; even on it the excess is exactly 20.0%, still not 'greater than 20%'. The absolute limb is met (2.39 km > 0.8 km), but both limbs must pass and the percentage limb does not. No route deviation is established, and POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

Billing integrity. POL-RD-09(4) is the only money route that survives a failed establishment test. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02817) carries no ERP gantry lines, no tolls and no airport surcharge, and every line reconciles to meter arithmetic — SGD 3.80 base fare, 14.4 km at SGD 0.75/km (SGD 10.80), 18.7 min at SGD 0.28/min (SGD 5.24) and the SGD 0.80 platform fee, totalling SGD 20.64. There is no unmatched or phantom charge line, so nothing is refundable under POL-RD-09.

The refund the rider asked for. The rider's advocate computed a POL-RD-02 refund of SGD 2.56 — recomputed fare SGD 18.08 (3.80 + 0.75 x 12.0 + 0.28 x 16.0 + 0.80, read with the fare breakdown's surge multiplier of 1.0), refund 20.64 - 18.08 = 2.56, payable SGD 2.60. That is correct as arithmetic but it is conditional on the establishment test being satisfied, and it is not. The SGD 2.60 is therefore not payable. (For completeness, the de minimis floor of SGD 0.50 and the 90% full-refund share would not have altered that figure had the gate been passed.)

Exclusions. None applies. The chat log (EV-CHAT-02817) holds 0 messages, so there is no rider instruction capable of engaging POL-RD-04; neither pickup_amended_at nor dropoff_amended_at is set and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 cannot re-apply the threshold against amended endpoints; and vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply and 12.0 km remains the only optimal on the record.

The driver's explanation. The driver's statement — 'Minor detour because of a road works sign' — asserts an external traffic cause. Under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-03 that assertion is tested against the traffic advisory for this trip and nothing else. No advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-02817-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT. The comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08; it neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal. This is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation, because the driver named no evidence ID for any advisory, so no exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited artifact. The statement is also not a measurement and cannot establish a deviation the numeric gate does not.

Profile material. The excess is not MATERIAL (2.39 km is neither more than 50% of optimal nor more than 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no conduct referral arises; in any event the only counters that clause names give driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d of 0 over completed_trips_90d of 174, far below its 0.05 / 40-trip test, so no pattern would be established. No other profile field bears on the outcome.

Trace integrity and escalation. The GPS trace is clean for policy purposes: 113 fixes, a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s. None of POL-RD-07(a)–(c) is met, so no independent corroboration is required and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifiers all match (TRP-02817); the timestamps are consistent; no exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited missing artifact; no refund computation arises to approach SGD 150.00; there is no mutually contradictory evidence of comparable strength; and no charge line lacks a counterpart. On confidence (POL-GEN-02(2)) the deciding fact — that the excess falls below the POL-RD-01 threshold — is carried by the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02817) and the trip record (EV-TRIP-02817), each at weight_multiplier 1.0, and the only impaired artifact is the missing advisory at 0.0, which carries no fact. Confidence is 0.90, comfortably above the 0.70 floor, so POL-RD-10(1) does not apply either.

POL-GEN-03: NO_ACTION is party-relative. On this rider-filed dispute, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so that state is left exactly as it is. Under POL-GEN-05 the monetary effect is nil, below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, and nothing is held.

The monetary effect is nil, below the execution threshold, so nothing is executed or held. No clause produces a referral on these facts."
  },
  "discarded_claims": []
}

ruling.explanation: To both parties: the disputed trip (TRP-02817) ran 14.39 km on the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02817) against a booked optimal of 12.0 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-02817), a measured excess of 2.39 km. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern and requires BOTH limbs of the establishment test to pass: the excess must be greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km. The absolute limb passes (2.39 km), but the percentage limb does not: 2.39 km is 19.92% of 12.0 km, below the 20% gate. The trip record's rounded 14.4 km would give exactly 20.0% — still not 'greater than 20%', and in any event not the governing field. No route deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED, and POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The 2.39 km excess is exactly the kind of minor detour the POL-RD-01 gate excludes from being refundable. The trace is clean for policy purposes — 113 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s — so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is met, no independent corroboration is required and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. The only surviving route to money on a failed establishment test is a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4), and there is nothing to correct: the fare ledger (EV-FARE-02817) carries no ERP gantry lines, no tolls and no airport surcharge, and every charge line reconciles to the trip record. The driver's note of a 'minor detour because of a road works sign' is not weighed: no traffic advisory covers this window (EV-ADVIS-02817-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0), so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and, under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08, an uncited traffic assertion neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal; it equally does not create a deviation the numeric gate does not find. The rider's quantified alternative — a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 2.60 computed under POL-RD-02 (recomputed_fare 18.08 against charged_total 20.64) — never runs, because POL-RD-02 applies only where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01. The rider's request to escalate on confidence grounds does not fire: the deciding facts (the trace distance and the booked optimal) are carried by the unimpaired GPS trace and trip record, each at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0 and the ruling is well above the 0.70 floor; POL-RD-10(5) and (7) are also not engaged, as the driver cited no advisory identifier and the rider's own figures concede the gate fails. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION leaves the state exactly as it is: fare_breakdown.payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 stand, and the disputed SGD 3.00 is not refunded. The monetary effect is zero, below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so no amount is held for reviewer release.

Both parties agree on the decisive arithmetic, and so do I. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess distance is BOTH greater than 20% of the optimal route AND greater than 0.8 km. The governing measurement is gps_trace.trace_distance_km on EV-GPS-02817: 14.39 km against the 12.0 km optimal on EV-TRIP-02817. That is an excess of 2.39 km — it clears the absolute limb (2.39 > 0.8 km), but it is 19.92% of optimal, which is not 'greater than 20%'. The percentage limb fails, and because POL-RD-01 requires both limbs, no deviation is established. Using the trip record's rounded 14.4 km would give exactly 20.0%, still not 'greater than 20%'; POL-RD-01 in any event forbids citing that rounded copy for the threshold test. The margin is small (about 10 m over a 14.39 km trace), but both of the platform's own distance figures fall on the same side of the gate, so the result is not genuinely in doubt. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 113 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s, so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) are not met, no independent corroboration is required, and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. No exculpatory clause changes the result and none is needed: the chat log EV-CHAT-02817 holds 0 messages (no POL-RD-04 rider instruction); neither pickup nor dropoff was amended and amended_optimal_distance_km is null (POL-RD-05 inapplicable); and vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL (POL-RD-12 inapplicable), so 12.0 km remains the only optimal on the record. The driver's counterparty note — 'Minor detour because of a road works sign' — is an uncited traffic-cause assertion. No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-02817-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and, under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13, the assertion neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal. Because the driver names no evidence ID for any advisory, POL-RD-13(1) treats this as a gap in the bundle rather than the POL-RD-10(5) contradiction, so it does not escalate the case. No billing-integrity correction is available under POL-RD-09(4): the fare ledger EV-FARE-02817 shows no ERP gantry lines, no tolls and no airport surcharge, and every line is meter arithmetic on the driven distance and time (14.4 km at $0.75/km plus 18.7 min at $0.28/min plus the $0.80 platform fee, surge multiplier 1.0 read from the fare breakdown). I have considered the rider's escalation request under POL-RD-10(1). The deciding fact — the 14.39 km trace on EV-GPS-02817 against the 12.0 km optimal on EV-TRIP-02817 — is carried by two independent weight-1.0 artifacts, so my confidence is capped at 1.0 and I am well above the 0.70 floor; POL-RD-10(1) is therefore not engaged. No other limb of POL-RD-10 fires either: identifiers match across all three artifacts (TRP-02817), no timestamps conflict or run backwards, the refund caps are nowhere near, and there is no mutually contradictory evidence of comparable strength — both sides read the same arithmetic to the same result. The rider's conditional refund computation (recomputed fare 18.08, refund 2.56, payable 2.60) is correct arithmetic but is never reached, because POL-RD-02 only runs once a deviation is established and it is not. Ruling: NO_ACTION. The rider's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state stands — the charge on EV-FARE-02817 (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is left exactly as it is. No amount is refunded, no driver compensation is payable, and no clause produces a referral (POL-RD-06(c) needs a MATERIAL deviation and a driver pattern, neither of which exists; POL-RD-09(4) finds no phantom line). The disputed SGD 3.00 remains charged; the monetary effect (zero) is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold, and this ruling is provisional with the POL-GEN-04 appeal route available to either party.

ledger.claim: The artifacts that carry the distance question all describe one and the same trip: trip_id TRP-02817 appears on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown alike; the trace's first fix (2026-08-10T07:28:09+08:00) is the recorded trip_started timestamp, and the fare was charged at 07:47:14, after the recorded trip end at 07:46:49. The rider's identification limb under POL-RD-08 is satisfied on the platform's own telemetry.

The rider pleaded the governing field, and the governing field confirms the detour: POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the measure, the trace runs 14.39 km against the 12.0 km optimal stored on the trip record, and the excess is 2.39 km. The trip record's 14.4 km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and under POL-RD-01 may not be cited for the threshold test; the rider has not cited it.

The establishment test is not met on the field as published, and the rider does not pretend otherwise: the trace excess of 2.39 km clears the absolute limb (well above 0.8 km) but is 19.92% of the 12.0 km optimal, some 10 metres short of the 20% limb, so POL-RD-01's percentage test fails and no deviation is established. The rider does not ask the tribunal to read 19.92% as 'greater than 20%', and does not press a distance refund as of right.

The driver's only explanation — "Minor detour because of a road works sign" — cannot be weighed, and I disclose the impairment on its face: no traffic advisory covers this trip, EV-ADVIS-02817-01 being MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT. POL-RD-03 therefore cannot be run, no closure-adjusted optimal can be produced, and under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08 an uncited traffic assertion neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended route; the driver names no artifact and no clause at all.

Nothing on this record excludes any part of the measured excess. The chat log holds 0 messages, so there is no rider instruction capable of engaging POL-RD-04; neither pickup_amended_at nor dropoff_amended_at is set and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 does not re-apply the threshold against amended endpoints; and vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply and 12.0 km remains the only optimal on the record.

If the tribunal finds the establishment test satisfied, the refund is arithmetic and is 2.56 before rounding: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 12.0 + 0.28 x 16.0) x 1.0 — the surge multiplier read from the fare breakdown, which is where POL-RD-02 says it must be read — plus 0.80 platform fee, nil ERP, nil fixed surcharge, nil waiting fee, less nil promo, giving 18.08; refund = 20.64 - 18.08 = 2.56, payable rounded up to SGD 2.60.

That refund is neither de minimis nor full: 2.56 is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so this is not a NO_ACTION case on quantum, and it is 12.4% of the 20.64 charged, below the 90% share that would make it a FULL_REFUND; it is also far below the SGD 150 figure that forces escalation under POL-RD-10. On that arithmetic the rider's ask is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 2.60 out of the SGD 3.00 contested.

No corroboration burden beyond the trace attaches to the rider's claim under POL-RD-08: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the four-or-more claims / one-or-fewer substantiated combination that would require independent corroboration for a sub-30% excess is simply not present here.

If the tribunal cannot reach confidence of 0.70 or better on a NO_ACTION ruling, POL-RD-10(1) requires ESCALATE, and on an escalation under POL-GEN-03 the disputed SGD 3.00 is held rather than collected — a materially better position for the rider than a ruling that leaves the whole 20.64 charged. The margin is exactly the size that makes that confidence arguable: the gate turns on a 10-metre shortfall measured over 113 fixes sampled every 10 seconds with no gaps, and the platform's own two published figures for the same distance (14.39 km and 14.4 km) differ by 0.01 km.

The deviation gate has two limbs and the percentage limb fails. Under POL-RD-01 the governing measurement is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which is 14.39 km against a booked optimal of 12.0 km, an excess of 2.39 km, or 19.92% of optimal. 19.92% is not 'greater than 20%', so no route deviation is ESTABLISHED, and POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip, save for the billing-integrity route under POL-RD-09(4) which is not in play here.

The rider's own headline figures prove the shortfall rather than the deviation. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure of 14.39 km govern over the trip record's 14.4 km, which is a rounded convenience copy that may not be cited for the threshold test; and even on that rounded copy the excess is exactly 2.40 km, precisely 20.0% of 12.0 km, which is still not 'greater than 20%'. On either figure the percentage limb fails.

I concede the absolute limb: 2.39 km does exceed the 0.8 km floor in POL-RD-01. But POL-RD-01 requires BOTH tests to pass, and only one does. A single satisfied limb cannot carry the rider's case, and the missing limb, the percentage limb, cannot be supplied from anything on this record.

The excess is not MATERIAL either, so the heavier machinery of POL-RD-06 is never engaged: 2.39 km is neither more than 50% of optimal nor more than 8.0 km absolute. Were the driver-profile check engaged it would find nothing to act on: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 174, a rate of 0.00, far below the 0.05 threshold and the 40-trip floor.

The trace is clean and unimpaired for policy purposes, so this case can be ruled on it without any of the gap-handling consequences. It carries 113 fixes over roughly 18 minutes 40 seconds at a 10-second sample interval, with 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. None of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is met, no independent corroboration is required, and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The initial burden is the rider's and it is not discharged. POL-RD-08 requires the rider to show, citing evidence, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold. The only artifacts that measure this trip, the trace and the booking optimal, put the excess at 2.39 km and 19.92%, below the threshold, so the burden never shifts to the driver and the driver need not reach any exculpatory clause at all.

The only route to money that survives a failed establishment test is a pass-through or billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09, and there is nothing to correct. The fare ledger shows no ERP gantry lines, no tolls and no airport surcharge, and no charge line lacking a counterpart in the trip record: it is meter arithmetic on 14.4 km at $0.75 per km plus 18.7 minutes at $0.28 per minute plus the $0.80 platform fee. POL-RD-09(4) affords the rider nothing on these facts.

NO_ACTION is both the correct outcome and, in this dispute, the outcome favourable to the driver. The dispute is rider-filed, and the fare breakdown records payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00. POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative and leaves that state exactly as it is: the charge stands and no money moves to the rider.

The driver's counterparty note that there was a minor detour because of a road works sign is not offered as an exoneration and does not alter the arithmetic: a minor detour is exactly what a 2.39 km, 19.92% excess looks like. A narrative sentence in a party statement is not a measurement and cannot substitute for the POL-RD-01 test or establish a deviation the trace does not show.
